introduction: The Lattice engine evaluates candidate wording against meaning supplied by the caller. Text to Lattice is a separate hosted service that starts with ordinary prose, proposes a rewrite, and checks whether it preserves the passage’s meaning.

subjects.name: Lattice method and engine
emphasis: Preserve what a passage says while changing how it reads.
Keep required instructions explicit across registers and accessible channels.
capabilities: Represent facts, obligations and their relationships in a caller-supplied meaning contract.
Test candidate wording against that contract, prioritize protected meaning, and record the selection in a derivation receipt.

subjects.name: Text to Lattice API
emphasis: Let visitors try a register change on a short passage and compare the result with their original.
Give visitors control over external processing and bound the cost of each request.
capabilities: Accept prose after confirmation, infer its meaning, and send drafting and review to designated models.
Check the proposed wording, return a translation or an already-suitable result, and withhold drafts that fail review.

evidence.subject: lattice-method
evidence.title: A change of tone can preserve an instruction
evidence.observation: In this illustration, “Return the key by Friday” becomes “Please return the key by Friday.” The tone shifts while the action and deadline stay the same. Moving the deadline to Monday would change the instruction. These sentences were written for this guide.

evidence.subject: lattice-method
evidence.title: The caller supplies the meaning to preserve
evidence.observation: The published method assigns the caller responsibility for the intended meaning. The engine evaluates wording against that contract and returns a record of its decision. The skill map describes the responsibility the host keeps when it presents the result.

evidence.subject: text-to-lattice-api
evidence.title: The service infers meaning from visitor prose
evidence.observation: After confirmation, the browser sends the passage to hah.dev. The Worker uses Qwen to analyze and draft, deterministic checks to screen the draft, and Llama to review it. A failed check can withhold the result. The hosted service implements its own inference pipeline.

evidence.subject: text-to-lattice-api
evidence.title: Consent and admission bound each submission
evidence.observation: Until the visitor confirms external processing, typing stays in the browser. Ordinary service admits 30 transformations globally and three per cooperating browser cookie jar each UTC day. The external services apply their own data-handling terms.

evidence.subject: text-to-lattice-api
evidence.title: Safari and Brave completed the visitor path
evidence.observation: In run 729, Safari returned a translation. Brave found its original passage already suited to the context. Each browser sent one content-bearing request to hah.dev, focused the result, and cleared the input and output on a hard reload. Firefox separately passed 14 input-only checks.

evidence.subject: text-to-lattice-api
evidence.title: The qualified build reached production
evidence.observation: On November 23, the production service check returned HTTP 200 and accepted the original wording. The subsequent Pages recovery published the build from that check. The two runs record the service result and the publication separately.

documents.subject: lattice-method
documents.question: What must a rewrite preserve?
documents.answer: Compare a direct request to return a key by Friday with a more courteous version. The tone may change. The action and deadline must survive. The public map explains how a caller states those requirements.
documents.title: Lattice concept and ecosystem map

documents.subject: lattice-method
documents.question: What can the engine decide?
documents.answer: The caller supplies the intended meaning. The engine assesses proposed wording and returns a decision record. Follow the public skill map to see which judgments still belong to the host.
documents.title: Lattice system skill map

documents.subject: text-to-lattice-api
documents.question: What happens after I submit?
documents.answer: The visitor confirms processing. The Worker checks admission, asks Qwen to analyze and draft, then checks the result with Llama. The terminal presents an accepted outcome or explains that the service withheld it.
documents.title: Text to Lattice service blueprint

documents.subject: text-to-lattice-api
documents.question: Where does my passage go, and what bounds the risk?
documents.answer: Typing stays local until confirmation. hah.dev then sends the passage through Hugging Face and OpenRouter to the named providers. Admission limits constrain work, the application avoids storing passage content, and a hard reload clears the visitor’s text.
documents.title: Text to Lattice security model
